question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4}\,,\,\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}⟩,t\in (-\infty ,0)$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨1\,,\,4⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3}\,,\,{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $⟨1\,,\,4⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨1\,,\,4⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨1\,,\,4⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨1\,,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨4{t}^{3}\,,\,{t}^{2}⟩ & =0 \\ 1\cdot 4{t}^{3}+4\cdot {t}^{2} & =0 \\ 4{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2} & =0 \\ 4{t}^{2}(t+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (-\infty ,0)$, the only solution is $t=-1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨{(-1)}^{4}\,,\,\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}⟩=⟨1\,,\,-\frac{1}{3}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $⟨1\,,\,4⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(1\,,\,-\frac{1}{3}).$
